problem: 'Re tells you which regime to expect before you open the valve' is misleading: Re needs the mean velocity V, and V is set by the valve opening (or by the design discharge). Before the valve is set you do not have V.
fix: The Reynolds number Re, computed from the velocity you set, tells you which regime to expect, so you can choose the right friction law before you read the dye.

problem: The apparatus list leaves out the bell-mouth (trumpet-shaped) entrance and the stilling arrangements (honeycomb/screens, settling time) that keep inlet disturbances low. Without them the dye line breaks up early and the lower critical Re falls well below 2000, which is exactly why the chapter later says the switch is not sharp.
fix: Add one line: the glass tube is fitted with a smooth bell-mouth entry and the water is left to settle, so inlet disturbances stay small and the transition occurs near Re ≈ 2000.

problem: 'The velocity profile is a paraboloid' can confuse a student into thinking of a 3-D surface; the exam point is the parabolic variation of u with radius, u = u_max(1 − r²/R²).
fix: Write: the velocity profile is parabolic, u = u_max(1 − r²/R²), where r is the distance from the centre (0 at the axis, R at the wall) and u_max is the centre-line velocity.
